Inspected previously indexed findings concern discrete visits or stationary interarrival observations rather than this first-detection model and interventions. Historical priority remains provisional.

value.rationale: Time-to-first detection is an ecologically motivated low-storage observable; the theorem proves a strict impossibility at a single setting for initially unavailable targets and identifies a less apparent quasi-stationary blind initialization even when initial availability is positive and known. It supplies an actionable design-level mathematical remedy—two calibrated sensor intensities—and exact minimal moment summaries when initial sites are empty; it clarifies what extra data, rather than merely more of the same data, separates arrival, departure and detectability. Practical calibration and finite-sample robustness remain unproved.
